data.name: Pollyanna
data.gender_notes: Pollyanna is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: A girl filled with optimism and enthusiasm
data.long_meaning: Pollyanna is a character created by Eleanor H. Porter in her 1899 novel of the same name. The term was later popularized in American culture as a synonym for a person who maintains a sunny and optimistic attitude despite adversity. The name Pollyanna carries the meaning “A girl filled with optimism and enthusiasm” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English. Parents who choose Pollyanna usually hope their child will grow to embody a girl filled with optimism and enthusiasm and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power of positive thinking and optimism

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pollyanna total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual sense, Pollyanna embodies the belief that even in the darkest of times, there is always a reason to hope and a reason to smile. Her unwavering faith in the goodness of people and the world around her reflects the teachings of many spiritual and religious traditions, which emphasize the importance of maintaining a positive attitude and trusting in the power of love and compassion to overcome adversity. Ultimately, Pollyanna's story reminds us that even when we encounter challenges and hardships, there is always a reason to believe in the power of redemption and the ability to find joy and meaning in the world around us.
